context: Evaluate a solution that adds in-person meeting detection to DetectMeetings based on sustained mic-only speech, with configurable thresholds and priority yielding to virtual meetings.

checklist.name: in_person_meetings_detected
checklist.description: DetectMeetings returns at least one meeting when mic speech is sufficiently dense and sustained, with no system audio present.
checklist.example: With mic speech at 60% of a 5-minute window for 10 minutes, DetectMeetings returns one meeting.

checklist.name: in_person_meeting_distinct_label
checklist.description: In-person meetings are distinguishable from virtual meetings in the returned Meeting values (e.g., a distinct App field).
checklist.example: Ground truth uses App: InPersonApp ("In person") as the label for detected in-person meetings.

checklist.name: sparse_speech_rejected
checklist.description: Mic activity that is too sparse or too brief does not produce an in-person meeting — detection has a minimum density and duration threshold.
checklist.example: ~8% mic speech ratio over 30 minutes produces no meeting; dense speech lasting only 3 minutes produces no meeting.

checklist.name: system_speech_alone_rejected
checklist.description: System audio alone (no mic speech) does not produce an in-person meeting.
checklist.example: A SpeechSpan with Track=="system" covering 20 minutes results in zero meetings from DetectMeetings.

checklist.name: yields_to_virtual_meetings
checklist.description: When a detected in-person region overlaps an already-detected virtual meeting (app-based or two-way-speech), the in-person meeting does not duplicate it — the virtual meeting takes priority.
checklist.example: Dense mic speech during an active Zoom session produces one meeting with App=="zoom.us", not two meetings.

checklist.name: two_way_speech_not_in_person
checklist.description: Concurrent mic and system speech (indicating a call) is treated as a virtual meeting, not an in-person meeting.
checklist.example: When mic and system speech both run for 20 minutes, DetectMeetings returns a call meeting, not an InPersonApp meeting.

checklist.name: screen_state_irrelevant
checklist.description: In-person detection fires even when the computer is locked or idle — the detection is based on mic speech, not computer activity.
checklist.example: Mic speech during loginwindow/KindIdle segments still produces an in-person meeting.

checklist.name: config_knobs_respected
checklist.description: Two new configuration knobs control detection: a minimum meeting duration and a minimum speech density ratio. Adjusting them changes detection outcomes as expected.
checklist.example: Lowering InPersonSpeechRatio from 0.4 to 0.25 causes a previously-missed 30%-dense meeting to be detected; raising InPersonMinMinutes drops short meetings.

checklist.name: config_struct_and_defaults
checklist.description: New config knobs follow the existing Config struct and Default() pattern: fields added to config.Config, defaults set in Default(), validation added in Validate() with sensible bounds.
checklist.example: InPersonMinMinutes and InPersonSpeechRatio added as typed fields with TOML tags; Default() sets them to 5 and 0.4; Validate() rejects out-of-range values.

checklist.name: config_example_documented
checklist.description: New config fields are documented in config.example.toml with a comment explaining their purpose and valid range.
checklist.example: config.example.toml gains in_person_min_minutes and in_person_speech_ratio entries with inline range comments.

checklist.name: detect_meetings_signature_unchanged
checklist.description: The public DetectMeetings function signature is not changed — in-person detection is added within the existing function, not as a separate entry point.
checklist.example: DetectMeetings(segs []Segment, speech []SpeechSpan, c config.Config) []Meeting — same signature, now also returns in-person meetings.

checklist.name: nearby_in_person_regions_merged
checklist.description: Two qualifying in-person regions separated by a short gap (less than 2 minutes) are merged into one meeting; a longer gap keeps them as separate meetings.
checklist.example: Two dense mic blocks with ~90s gap become one meeting; the same blocks with a 10-minute gap become two meetings.

checklist.name: config_validation_bounded
checklist.description: The new config values are validated against sensible bounds — values outside the valid range are rejected by Validate().
checklist.example: InPersonMinMinutes=0 or 121 causes Validate() to return an error; InPersonSpeechRatio=0.04 or 1.01 likewise.

checklist.name: commit_type_is_feat
checklist.description: The commit message in `COMMIT_MSG.txt` uses the Conventional Commits format and the type is `feat`, because the change adds new behavior: in-person meetings are now detected and logged.
checklist.example: feat(activity): detect in-person meetings from mic activity

checklist.name: commit_subject_rules
checklist.description: The first line of `COMMIT_MSG.txt` is in the imperative mood, starts with a lowercase letter after the type prefix, has no trailing period, and is at most 72 characters including the type prefix.
checklist.example: 'feat(activity): detect in-person meetings from mic activity' passes; 'Added stuff.' fails (past tense, capitalized, trailing period, no type).

checklist.name: commit_not_run
checklist.description: The agent stages the changes and writes the proposed message to `COMMIT_MSG.txt`, but does not run `git commit`.
checklist.example: `COMMIT_MSG.txt` exists at the repo root; `git log` has no new commit.
